prs-crc.body:
## Hold: whole-import benefit remains unqualified

All **69 timing reports**, **24 memory observations** and **2,435 raw process-tree scans** independently reconcile. Correctness, output, storage and media checks pass; the performance result remains inconclusive.

| Corpus | B/A paired median [descriptive 95% interval] | B/C paired median [interval] |
| --- | --- | --- |
| JMdict | +1.085% [−0.491%, +2.929%] | +0.301% [−1.597%, +2.104%] |
| Jitendex | −1.186% [−1.719%, −0.220%] | −0.792% [−4.041%, +0.103%] |
| VNDB | +0.859% [−4.536%, +3.886%] | +0.131% [−8.671%, +4.740%] |

Negative changes mean faster. Jitendex's comparison with C crosses zero; the screen does not establish a reliable material gain. The worst VNDB identical-product C/A pair (+10.625%) remains included.

JMdict and Jitendex pass both memory replications. VNDB fails both because five observations exceed the fixed 250 ms covered-scan-gap limit: ABBA gaps 330.483, 266.171, 322.760 and 370.240 ms; BAAB B2 gap 452.155 ms. Those qualified peaks and replication medians remain null. One unreadable address-space scan is retained and conservatively excluded. These coverage failures do not establish a measured memory regression, but they prevent a passing qualification.

**Keep draft.** No retry, replacement observation, discarded outlier or threshold change is used to obtain a favorable result. The local full-concurrency VNDB process exits remain recorded separately from the successful bounded parity replay.

### Archived current-source evidence

[Evidence PR #923](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/pull/923) · [Immutable study index](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/blob/ae6b76235b5a913867748de377c996eaf91c0e7f/builds/perf/import-20261125-2754/README.md). The archive preserves original observations, failures, source/package identities, portable audits, component receipts and validation logs. Each candidate and frozen acquisition is identified separately; later validation heads do not relabel measured results.

---

## Problem

The compressed native parser can reuse a glossary CRC only when it already has an exact byte-equality witness. The existing verifier splits CRC work at every unique row and applies a compression-ratio admission gate, so the pinned Jitendex workload still rechecks most glossary source bytes.

## Change

Keep each uninterrupted run of original source bytes contiguous and compute a separate glossary CRC only for an equality root that another row actually references. Flatten witness chains in the existing witness array, then reuse those proven CRCs. Incremental braided CRC accepts the preceding CRC state, with a small input-independent polynomial-power table.

The source-size and deflate constraints remain. Remove the compression-ratio admission gate so the same exact verifier can apply to low-compression groups. Original source CRC verification, exact equality, bank boundaries, monotonic row-span validation and errors before delivery to the sink remain enforced.

This creates no additional per-row verifier table. **Broader eligibility does activate the existing four-byte-per-reserved-row witness allocation for more inputs**, so memory remains a qualification gate.

## Validation

- Changed-file ESLint, main/test TypeScript and all seven dry-build targets pass.
- **Full unit suite: 14,567 passed, 47 skipped across 647 passing files** on the frozen product source. The source-CRC and contiguous-run cases and CRC matrix tests pass. Pinned LLVM 21.1.8 source-bound WASM reproduction passes.
- New tests cover overlapping/backward ranges, zero-length spans, bank crossings, interleaved witnesses and chains, long unique runs, exact braided-CRC boundaries, and corruption outside reused spans.
- A newly admitted stored bank over 4 MiB verifies low-compression admission and rejects a bad source CRC before sink delivery.
- Exact production-worker output parity passes for **201 groups / all 7,613,164 rows** across JMdict, Jitendex and VNDB, including content slabs, metadata, interned plans, prepared indexes, route filters and media. VNDB uses the identical 170 production-group partition with bounded sequential worker lifetimes; that establishes output parity, not normal-concurrency memory qualification.
- Independent native-code review found no correctness blocker; its two requested boundary/corruption regressions are included.
- Source-bound WASM regenerated with LLVM 21.1.8; 63,004 → 63,334 bytes (+330).
- The earlier candidate full-concurrency VNDB harness exited 137. Its cause is not established and it remains a failed acquisition. Subsequent bounded correctness replay does not establish a passing concurrent-memory result. Hosted source CI and the separate browser memory study remain required.

### Latest source CI snapshot

[Final-head source CI](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/actions/runs/45650131440) remains incomplete: the test build, Firefox extension E2E, Anki matrix and dev TypeScript pass; the other eleven required jobs are queued. The separate [Chromium restart workflow](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/actions/runs/45650131436) passes. [CodeQL](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/actions/runs/45650131540) failed after query evaluation and SARIF export, during result upload. The available logs do not establish the exact cause; this remains an unresolved failed gate. These statuses do not replace the complete local validation receipts or the frozen performance outcomes.

## Performance status

**Draft: complete-import speed and memory are not yet qualified.** A local diagnostic Jitendex component run preserved all outputs and avoided CRC scans of 161,688,452 out of 538,927,310 source bytes in the actual 22 production groups. No end-to-end speed percentage is claimed from component timings.

The measured candidate is frozen against develop `7d1643e6147a10cb2165e9744cf0e63b59e46632`, at `c2cf7647c67b02474301ed48e54a53205be0f027` (tree `074e622aec0c6537c7f0d8ac92725dd62c28b73b`). [Hosted timing screens](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/actions/runs/45644628634) compare separately built release packages on all three pinned dictionaries, with identical-product controls, fresh profiles, complete import through UI completion, restart/lookup/media/storage checks and retained failures. [Separate PSS/private-memory cohorts](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/actions/runs/45644635208) check the broadened witness eligibility on all three dictionaries.

Latest PR head `2fe47fa3db04342d04eb4f309c5d74ef45eef9e3` (tree `18f2494dbb185f189c59efb8ba2b1bf96855eeb8`) adds one JSDoc descriptor annotation in a test, fixing the test-type gate. All shipped product files remain byte-identical to the frozen measured source. Test TypeScript and scoped lint pass after that annotation; no benchmark cohort was repeated.

This is distinct from prior per-row CRC prototypes: unique source spans stay contiguous and unused roots are not separately hashed. No worker, batch, cache, compression-level or dictionary threshold was tuned. No third-party implementation code was copied.

prs-crc.title: perf: reduce short-gap CRC work with existing slicing tables
prs-crc.body:
**Held component-only draft.** The CRC-stage evidence supports reviewing this small implementation, but the active VNDB browser trial has adverse complete-import timing and fails memory-coverage qualification. No browser non-regression or merge-readiness claim is made.

## Why

The incremental source-gap CRC helper consumes full 16-byte blocks, then handles every remaining byte serially. VNDB has many short gaps between exact raw spans covered by CRC witnesses, so those dependent tail steps are a recurring cost even when most source bytes are already covered.

## Change

Use the existing slicing tables for an optional eight-byte tail and then an optional four-byte tail, leaving at most three scalar bytes. This adds 25 production C lines, with no new table or allocation and no change to witness selection, group sizing, admission, persisted formats, or CRC semantics.

The checked-in parser WASM and native manifest are regenerated with the pinned Clang/LLD 21.1.8 toolchain. The WASM grows by 284 bytes; the CRC helper is the only changed production function body. A test-only export permits an independent Node-zlib oracle over 8,160 combinations of input length, alignment and preceding CRC state.

## Measured benefit and limits

This is a component optimization. It does not establish a complete-browser import speedup.

| Measurement                                                                         | Result                                                                               | Scope                                                                                                           |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Captured-gap replay, 120,012 spans from the first 12 VNDB banks, 24 balanced blocks | Paired CRC-only improvement of 21.21%; medians 103.97 → 82.49 ms for sixteen repeats | Exploratory selection screen; concatenates gaps into one CRC state and excludes the verifier's combination work |
| Complete sequential VNDB parser, all 665 banks / 6,648,310 rows, first order        | Summed CRC phase 62.01 ms lower, or 8.65%                                            | All compared parser outputs exact; unchanged inflation also improves                                            |
| Same complete corpus, reverse initial order                                         | Summed CRC phase 49.87 ms lower, or 6.82%                                            | Supports a CRC-stage signal, without attributing the enclosing parser change                                    |
| Selected direct production-verifier replay                                          | Geometric change −3.19%; descriptive 95% interval [−7.38%, +1.74%]                   | Inconclusive; unchanged whole-bank control's equal-work time moves +3.89%                                       |

The local full-parser cohorts use 332 groups and scan 872 MB. The browser production census uses 170 groups and scans 568 MB across three workers. These percentages must not be applied to complete-browser time or summed worker durations. Wider slicing32 was slower in the complete parser; padding was inconclusive. Their observations remain in the evidence, including failed or incomplete attempts and the limits of retained acquisition-script provenance.

## Validation

- Hosted validation of the identical four product blobs passed on frozen study head `3080deb631a7536fabe8ccb2f77f8f55e11ef061` in [run 46107723369](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/actions/runs/46107723369): pinned native reproduction, full units, all-target build, scoped lint, and main/test types. This PR contains those four files; the study workflow stays on its experimental branch.
- The initial hosted run passed native reproduction, 669 unit files / 15,136 tests with 47 conditional skips, and builds, then failed test-only array formatting. The current trial changes only that formatting; runtime source and WASM bytes are unchanged. Both receipts are retained.
- The original three-corpus browser study is complete. All recorded semantic checks pass; the complete-import timings and VNDB memory-coverage failure are retained below.

## Completed browser screen: no whole-import gain

The frozen study `3080deb631a7536fabe8ccb2f77f8f55e11ef061` has the exact four product files in this PR. Both actual extension packages were audited; only the C source and generated WASM differ, with candidate WASM Git blob `dc1673cd501778a8a48e8faa4cc5c81076f2a19d`.

All 26 imports and semantic receipts per corpus pass. Negative changes are faster. These are the original six paired complete-import observations and two identical-code controls; no observations are excluded or adjusted.

| Corpus   | B/A paired median | Equal-work change | Descriptive 95% interval | Identical C/A median | Original memory gate                                                       |
| -------- | ----------------: | ----------------: | ------------------------ | -------------------: | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| JMdict   |          −0.1617% |          +0.0606% | [−0.6572%, +1.0069%]     |             +0.3091% | Pass; 303 raw scans                                                        |
| Jitendex |          +0.4451% |          +0.2622% | [−1.0960%, +1.4487%]     |             +0.4088% | Pass; 333 raw scans                                                        |
| VNDB     |          +4.6426% |          +6.4226% | [−0.9559%, +15.5290%]    |             +1.1104% | Fail; A2 coverage gap 295.200949 ms exceeds 250 ms; 482 raw scans retained |

JMdict and Jitendex have zero deferred-source CRC time/scanned/reused work in every report, so they are inactive-path controls for this change. VNDB is active, but four of six complete imports are slower, including the full +19.3509% sixth pair. Its memory failure is insufficient coverage, not a demonstrated memory regression; the comparison remains unqualified, with null aggregate maxima.

An **added secondary analysis**, requested at 07:50:20 UTC while VNDB was running and before its outcome was reviewed, describes the same six pairs and two controls. It is not a registered primary endpoint or new gate. All 16 observations have exactly 568,284,368 scanned bytes, 3,699,708,599 reused bytes and 6,490,145 reused glossaries. Summed worker `parserSourceCrcMs` is lower in all six candidate pairs: median −4.0486%, equal-work −4.0686%, descriptive interval [−5.4962%, −2.6251%]. Both identical-code phase controls also improve (−0.1508% and −4.3172%), limiting attribution. This timer covers the deferred verifier, not just its gap-tail helper, and is not import wall time. No control or phase time is subtracted from the primary result.

The earlier component benefit and this secondary phase observation support only a small held implementation review. **The complete browser study establishes no import gain or broad non-regression, fails VNDB memory qualification, and does not establish merge readiness.** The adverse VNDB timing remains part of the decision.

Original run: [46107723369](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/actions/runs/46107723369). The [completed browser readout](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/blob/c89af6f108eebab73dcdbc7c3a292c189a6161e6/dev/perf/import-evidence-20261128-1b47/crc-browser-addendum-README.md), [all raw evidence](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/blob/c89af6f108eebab73dcdbc7c3a292c189a6161e6/dev/perf/import-evidence-20261128-1b47/crc-browser-addendum-20261128-1b47.tar.gz), and [member hash manifest](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/blob/c89af6f108eebab73dcdbc7c3a292c189a6161e6/dev/perf/import-evidence-20261128-1b47/crc-browser-addendum-20261128-1b47.manifest.json) are preserved at immutable commit `c89af6f108eebab73dcdbc7c3a292c189a6161e6`. Archive SHA-256: `84d5ae1f80c2a5ccfb2981c71eb335b4320d09ec19c649884fb512e5a561d8c5`.

## Reproduction and evidence

The [scope and reproduction README](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/blob/3c3ba7600a8811df6b8631b72a0ac5379f8b60d1/dev/perf/import-evidence-20261128-1b47/crc8_4-README.md), [complete evidence archive](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/blob/3c3ba7600a8811df6b8631b72a0ac5379f8b60d1/dev/perf/import-evidence-20261128-1b47/crc8_4-evidence-20261128-1b47-v2.tar.gz), and [per-member hash manifest](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/blob/3c3ba7600a8811df6b8631b72a0ac5379f8b60d1/dev/perf/import-evidence-20261128-1b47/crc8_4-evidence-20261128-1b47-v2.manifest.json) are preserved at immutable evidence commit `3c3ba7600a8811df6b8631b72a0ac5379f8b60d1`. Archive SHA-256: `4d47af5543a594dfc4083efabfd568250dfc28d48f53e9361b53722f0d3dd823`.

The compact bundle includes the measured source/native checkpoints, current test file, frozen observations, independent oracle checks, scripts, input hashes, reconstruction instructions and rejected variants. Large dictionary archives and reproducible raw source captures are omitted with explicit hashes and recipes.

Original modifications to existing project code; no third-party source was imported.

prs-crc.title: perf: compact fused metadata for dictionary imports
prs-crc.body:
## Why

The strict fused import parser allocates a 17-word (68-byte) source metadata record for every row even after it has emitted the final content and numeric columns. JMdict, Jitendex and VNDB keep these records live through projection and lookup-index preparation.

## Changes

- Retain the seven words still needed after fused encoding: expression, reading and glossary spans plus media/sequence flags. This reduces that metadata allocation to 28 bytes per row, a 58.8% reduction in this component.
- Keep the existing four-row reuse policy with a five-row full-metadata ring. Ordinary object parsing, fallback parsing and experimental global exact-content reuse retain the full layout.
- Read compact glossary spans in the native source-CRC verifier and preserve media projection, including a source `-0` sequence.
- Place the existing retired row metadata and hash tables together, and permit lookup scratch to use aligned unused content/string tails. Live source, content, keys and numeric columns remain protected. This preserves native lookup admission after reducing the metadata allocation.
- Regenerate the pinned WASM and manifest with the repository's LLVM 21.1.8 toolchain.

## Validation

- 120 focused tests pass, including exact full-versus-compact output equality, reuse-window and bank boundaries, escaped keys, media, negative-zero sequence preservation, full-layout fallback, native segmented lookup, deferred source CRC and malformed sources.
- Sentinel tests verify lookup writes in retired tails cannot overwrite live source/content/key/numeric data, metadata, signatures or alignment gaps.
- Changed-file repository ESLint passes.
- Independent review caught and fixed negative-zero sequence loss; the final scratch layout and lifetime constraints were also reviewed.
- [Complete-corpus proof](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/blob/61e3e059c95b208e2167141e70488add99e3b1a7/test/perf/native-metadata-20261126-21d3/README.md) passes for JMdict (528,299 rows), Jitendex (436,555), and VNDB (6,648,310) under each existing 2-, 3-, and 5-worker grouping policy. All 616 groups preserve exact content/key/lookup/route/media/CRC output and native admission, with zero scratch misses or fused/native fallbacks.
- The evidence includes the exact measured probe, all raw successful and rejected attempts, source/fixture/WASM hashes, and an independent verifier. The nine complete replays use the frozen committed tree.
- [Hosted CI](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/actions/runs/45865210236) passes all 15 normal jobs on this exact source: **651 unit files / 14,681 tests passed**, 47 conditional skips, build, all type checks, lint, Chromium and Firefox. The pinned LLVM 21.1.8 rebuild and all seven extension targets also pass. Separate static-web, restart-interruption and CodeQL workflows pass.
- Local attempt records preserve the initial compiler-setup failures and unchanged hash-test timeouts. With the pinned compiler environment, all 21 compiler-dependent native tests pass. No assertion or timeout was changed. The exact-source hosted full suite closes the full-unit gate.
- [Exact-source validation receipts](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/blob/481f32470d43109c387ed8c657e0d4960bcdd1a3/test/perf/native-metadata-20261126-21d3/validation/README.md) bind all local and hosted records to the same product tree.
- The [corrected native comparison cohorts](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/actions/runs/45872657905) in #930 are running with the exact four packaged changes (the C source ships alongside the two JS files and WASM). The first native study stopped at package preflight before any warmup or timing observation; those failures remain preserved. This remains a draft while comparative performance qualification settles.

The 68-to-28-byte figure is a parser metadata allocation reduction. No whole-import latency or browser peak-memory improvement is claimed yet.

## Component memory result

Maximum WASM buffer capacity for the single parser instance in each three-worker **grouping** replay:

| Dictionary | Baseline | Candidate | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| JMdict | 43,384,832 B | 41,353,216 B | 2,031,616 B |
| Jitendex | 76,087,296 B | 71,237,632 B | 4,849,664 B |
| VNDB | 45,219,840 B | 43,646,976 B | 1,572,864 B |

These sequential component replays do not measure parallel browser scheduling or whole-process memory. The hosted A/B study remains separate.

## Source identity

Base: `0143e9596cd8f790d5e166d4ba6a2425fbc57f14`  
Published source: `0e233538e975c7be11b2144974923e2bf6396254`  
Tree: `c83e5d77135b1ccf8ab86a4c51065758e3038b5d`  
Pinned WASM SHA-256: `90d1d539ecf1e0f5519de9bc9aeab7ca550feb0c54e46bf411e93650d64ce264`

This change is independent of the VNDB media staging follow-up in #943 and does not alter worker-count, compression, cache or dictionary-selection policy.

## Problem

VNDB's generation-media index parses numeric image paths during construction, selection, and later reads. Each successful parse creates a substring and converts the parsed number back to a string to check canonical spelling. The locked VNDB source has 146,570 images.

## Change

Scan canonical decimal digits directly in the original path. Preserve the positive safe-integer domain and leave uint32 storage limits with the existing callers. Prefix/suffix matching, invalid-descriptor errors, empty-suffix behavior, slot layout, CRC validation, and index ownership remain unchanged.

## Result: retain as draft

The [complete-VNDB six-block screen](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/actions/runs/45262916933) passed every correctness check, but **does not establish a complete-import gain**.

| Candidate B / baseline A | +0.057% | −9.486% to +0.986% |
| Candidate B / identical baseline C | −0.268% | −2.562% to +0.989% |
| Identical baseline C / baseline A | +0.144% | −7.681% to +0.653% |

All 18 timed imports and two separate exhaustive-media diagnostics are retained. The slow first baseline observation and identical-code drift are included. The local component screen was also noisy. [Complete preserved evidence](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/blob/a4b7ba86fcffe90f9bfcd11d11999fae80c9b26f/docs/performance/import-crossover-20261123/REPORT.md) contains original artifacts, scripts, source identities, byte oracles, CI receipts, and unsuccessful local attempts alongside their successful recoveries.

## Provenance

prs-crc.body:
## Problem

Compressed dictionary sources spend parser work expanding DEFLATE history matches. The native decoder currently copies long matches in 8-byte words even though the pinned production WASM already enables SIMD.

## Change

Use interleaved 16-byte WASM loads and stores for fast-loop matches at distance 16 or greater, advancing 32 bytes per iteration. The forward copy order preserves overlapping matches; the maximum 31-byte overrun remains inside the existing fast-loop guard. Short-distance matches, the bounded tail, CRC checks, exact input consumption, output limits, and non-WASM builds retain their existing paths.

The generated parser grows by 62 bytes (54,596 → 54,658). The manifest and vendor provenance bind the reviewed change. Compression settings, source grouping, workers, and persisted formats are unchanged.

## Validation

- 86 focused production-WASM tests passed, covering malformed streams, CRC/size/trailing rejection, output-memory boundaries, overlap distances, and the maximum DEFLATE history distance.
- Every non-directory entry in the pinned JMdict, Jitendex, and VNDB archives matched both the baseline decoder and independent Node zlib: 5,169,815,579 decompressed bytes in total.
- Clang/LLD 21.1.8 regenerated the checked-in module reproducibly.
- Full CI and all other PR checks passed at the exact published runtime.

## Performance decision: HOLD

The complete browser study did **not** establish a repeatable whole-import improvement. This remains draft.

[Run 45119098795](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/actions/runs/45119098795) completed all 252 fresh-profile imports: six cells, each with six excluded warmups, twelve adjacent alternating AB/BA candidate pairs, six interleaved AC/CA same-code control pairs, and an independent reversed-order host. There were no failed imports or discarded measured observations. Timing ends at the post-UI import-complete event; restart checks and twelve source-derived persisted-content probes passed for every import.

Percentages below are median paired candidate/baseline changes; negative is faster. Control is a separate same-code C/A median and is not subtracted.

| Dictionary | Forward candidate | Forward control | Reversed candidate | Reversed control |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| JMdict | −1.97% | +0.66% | +0.64% | +0.98% |
| Jitendex | −0.65% | +0.85% | +0.90% | +1.26% |
| VNDB | +1.33% | +0.04% | +0.13% | +0.16% |

Every candidate median bootstrap interval crosses zero. The earlier fixed component screen also had large same-code drift; neither screen nor browser results justify a speed claim. All observations and failures are retained in the study artifacts and the evidence PR #814. The browser evidence covers Linux x64 Chromium; sampled persisted probes are not exhaustive equality, which is separately covered by the archive byte oracle above.

Source baseline: `5e1f8c12f7ff798ba407323aff675cb23b22af02`. Published runtime: `5555f3efd3e0c8baa99e93b4c14e7f1889c30383`, tree `a7c6e31bfb8449d9715916adb89cbf50b143bf2e`. Frozen study source: `1788fa1fe889c407d24d0f4b5ca23689946fbcec`.

prs-crc.title: Reduce media requirement allocation during dictionary imports
prs-crc.body:
## Problem

Projected dictionary images already own the diagnostic key bytes needed for errors, but import bookkeeping wraps those bytes in an entry object and clones the requirement again when deferring media. Dense ZIP setup also allocates a temporary assignment object per entry, and packed media copies and sorts its records even when they are already in physical archive order.

## Change

- Create one internal projected media requirement containing its path and owned diagnostic fields, and reuse it through deferred resolution.
- Attach the shared data reader directly to each private dense ZIP entry.
- Detect nondecreasing physical offsets during the existing validation pass. Reuse that record order when possible, retaining the sorted-copy fallback for other request orders.

The existing diagnostic-byte copy boundary, first-reference ordering, ordinary image target/getter behavior, cancellation, CRC checks, header/range validation and persistence format are preserved.

## Validation

- 140 focused tests passed, including immediate and deferred resolution, copied diagnostic keys after parser memory reuse, mixed projected/fallback references, first-reference errors, sorted/reversed/duplicate ZIP offsets, and cancellation joining an active read.
- Main/test TypeScript, scoped ESLint and the all-target build dry run passed.
- Independent review of this frozen change found no blocker.
- Full units, locked-corpus media parity, PR CI and frozen browser comparisons are in progress. This is a draft; no complete-import speedup or browser memory reduction is claimed yet.

Baseline: `d24b4e56ceb1fe14ad96ef3853f4d397efa6fa26`. Candidate: `ebb0777114578c5cee879877274e7d872bfea27e`. Source tree: `923cd36b875afbbee6e6674fd1b4450bed6ce362`.

Original changes to the repository's existing GPL-covered implementation; no third-party implementation code was added. This follows the existing projected-diagnostics path and is separate from the numeric media-path and direct media-entry proposals.

prs-crc.body:

## Current revision — November 27

This revises the existing ownership proposal on current develop, preserves its original commits, and keeps the earlier **HOLD** evidence below. The added optimization reuses the owned **Uint16 expression-ID column** at the immediate parser-worker transfer boundary. Generic copy-helper callers retain independent snapshots. The original retained-record key-arena safeguard is carried forward.

The additional expression column removes **30,452,656 bytes of cumulative allocations across the three current corpora**. Key-arena/key-length reuse is prior #820 work; the entire combined reduction is not a new discovery.

### Complete current-corpus proof

| Dictionary | Rows | Total cumulative buffers removed | Expression-column portion |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| JMdict | 528,299 | 10,434,868 B | **2,113,196 B** |
| Jitendex | 436,555 | 11,477,248 B | **1,746,220 B** |
| VNDB | 6,648,310 | 229,184,826 B | **26,593,240 B** |
| Total | 7,613,164 | 251,096,942 B | **30,452,656 B** |

These are actual unique emitted backing-buffer counts under the existing three-worker grouping, summed over the import. They are **not peak memory, bytes copied over IPC, or import-time savings**. The expression portion is the exact arithmetic `4 × whole-index rows`; it is not a separately timed key-only control.

The actual parser-worker handler, compressed-source inflate/CRC, real transfer list and structured-clone detachment pass full content/key/numeric/metadata/dedup/media/index parity under existing 2-, 3- and 5-worker groupings: **616 groups / 22,839,492 row comparisons**. Previous owned results survive later native heap reuse. The two-worker JMdict replay also covers the unchanged segmented path. Execution is sequential and does not model browser scheduling.

- Baseline: `9e10d3b3fcf66d344ab31bc42c9b522fa5215da2`.
- Current revision: `f65f4ef97ebf2f37a5b1b79ca7733d7b362ec963`; tree `9c34079709e7b8f6cae6b61c9ef537bb965ebcee`.
- [Exact source, raw evidence, failed attempts and reproduction index](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/tree/f65f4ef97ebf2f37a5b1b79ca7733d7b362ec963/builds/perf/import-owned-columns-83b3-evidence).
- [Experiment handoff](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/blob/f65f4ef97ebf2f37a5b1b79ca7733d7b362ec963/dev/perf/import-experiments-20260914.md).

### Validation and browser qualification

**22 focused tests, scoped strict TypeScript, scoped repository ESLint, and source whitespace checks pass.** [Static web acceptance](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/actions/runs/46103918233) also passed on the exact product tree: main/test/web types, 78 focused tests, and 24 no-extension browser scenarios covering full JMdict/Jitendex imports, restart, cancellation/recovery and offline lookup. [Actionlint](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/actions/runs/46103918146) and dependency review pass. [Normal CI](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/actions/runs/46103918118) is **fully passing: all 15 enabled gates**, including all four type projects, lint, both Chromium and Firefox full-extension E2E, the pinned native rebuild, the options suite, and the complete unit suite: **670 files / 15,152 tests passed, 47 existing skips**. Four conditional lanes were skipped, not counted as passes. The [registered performance qualification](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/actions/runs/46103918280) has finished all four cells and all 136 planned imports. Its final status is failure solely because VNDB candidate memory observation B1 did not meet the fixed sampling-coverage limit; the detailed HOLD decision is below. The native WASM is unchanged. The final corpus runner passed independent review; its earlier eager-diagnostic serialization failure and other failed attempts remain preserved and are excluded from performance interpretation.

The registered hosted study used two independent, opposite-order JMdict cells with **12 candidate pairs each**, plus six-pair Jitendex and VNDB cells. Each retains identical-code controls, fresh profiles, post-UI completion, persisted readback/restart checks, separate exhaustive media verification, and separate audited memory observations. Source/package guards permit exactly the parser, parser-worker and retained-record-store changes. No worker, grouping, compression, cache or dictionary policy is changed. A separate baseline JMdict trace is diagnostic only.

### Completed browser study: HOLD

The [complete raw evidence and independent readbacks for all four cells](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/tree/7a48cd9dea074d4d92f3456b4911c9e2aacdd744/builds/perf/import-owned-columns-83b3-hosted) are durably preserved, including every control, tail and raw memory scan. Only the original product ZIP payloads are excluded from the compact derivative archives; their verified complete inventories and digests remain. All non-package observations are retained.

Independent readback verifies every complete timing schedule, raw browser monotonic endpoint, exact source/package/fixture binding, all 2/3/5 component replay policies, post-UI readback/restart and exhaustive-media gate. The first three cells also pass separate memory qualification. VNDB's sole failed gate is memory coverage, described below. These results belong to current head `f65f4ef97ebf2f37a5b1b79ca7733d7b362ec963`; earlier historical cohorts remain separate.

Negative changes are faster. Each row is one host. Equal work compares summed matched durations. Identical-code C/A controls remain separate, without subtraction or host pooling.

| Cell | Candidate B/A median | Candidate equal work | Faster pairs | Identical C/A median | Identical C/A equal work |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| JMdict, initial AB | +0.2584% | +0.4499% | 6/12 | +1.0747% | +0.2374% |
| JMdict, initial BA | +0.0487% | +2.2435% | 6/12 | +1.2052% | +0.1371% |

| Cell | Sampled private-memory median change | Sampled PSS median change | Qualification |

The small Jitendex sampled-memory reduction is descriptive. JMdict does not show a memory reduction here. The deterministic cumulative allocation saving remains the concrete mechanism result.

### Further investigation and preserved evidence

[The complete follow-up evidence bundle](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/blob/bc26b191ba38d3b5cfd90d4c88584883720d267c/builds/perf/import-owned-columns-83b3-followup/README.md) preserves all 153 independently verified files: fixed request-batching and aligned-checksum cohorts, exact inputs, controls, failures, corrected canonical-sink profiles, complete native-symbol proof, and the compressed-input JMdict diagnostic. The historical executor-interruption snapshot is retained separately. The completed [baseline browser trace readback and additive sampling correction](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/tree/cf43df9f197b729085950dc9f2f7b3ee7a773e35/builds/perf/20261128-browser-jmdict-profile-83b3) preserve the full raw trace and correct the initial sampling-gap interpretation without modifying earlier raw archives. Separately, [#830](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/pull/830) now contains a current-source 17 ms direct-registration result and its own prospective browser qualification; it is not pooled with this ownership study.

**Status remains draft/HOLD.** The allocation reduction is concrete; the completed study does not establish a qualified complete-browser speed or exact peak-memory benefit. Historical results below belong to their original source and fixtures and will not be pooled with the current study.

<details>
<summary>Historical November 23 proposal and completed HOLD evidence — preserved unchanged</summary>

## Problem

Native whole-chunk lookup indexes already contain an owned UTF-8 key arena and key-length table. The parser result copies both again into its key plan before transfer, adding work and another backing allocation.

## Change

When the native producer owns the complete sidecar and row byte lists are omitted, let its key plan refer to those exact owned subviews. A private WeakMap witnesses the producer and descriptor identities. Replaced descriptors fall back to ordinary copying; in-place edits stay visible to the current validation path. Explicit row-byte-list callers keep their existing aliases and copying behavior. Segmented and arbitrary split plans retain their existing contracts.

Retained record caches detach one tightly sized key arena when keeping a subview would otherwise pin the whole prepared sidecar. Normal OPFS imports discard these materialized records and keep the copy reduction. No grouping, concurrency, compression, or persisted format changes.

## Correctness and work reduction

- Complete stable row/content/media/key-plan/index outputs match baseline for all 526,942 JMdict, 435,448 Jitendex and 6,648,310 VNDB rows.
- Summed duplicate copied bytes removed in the serial corpus partitions: **8,301,780 JMdict; 9,706,463 Jitendex; 202,591,586 VNDB**. These are copy/allocation-volume reductions, not peak-memory or elapsed-time claims. Partitions have production-shaped group counts; exact bank membership was not independently matched to the browser planner.
- 234 parser/boundary and 195 record-store tests passed. Ownership coverage includes detached/transferred buffers, source reuse, descriptor replacement, in-place edits, explicit byte lists and retained-cache backing-buffer size/mutation independence.
- Main types, scoped lint and all-target build dry runs passed. The local complete test-type process was killed with exit 137 and no diagnostics; that original failure remains retained. [Hosted full CI 45122913657 passed](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/actions/runs/45122913657), including the complete test-type gate, unit suites, pinned build, and Chromium/Firefox extension E2E. Optional workflow lanes were skipped, not represented as passes.
- Native WASM is unchanged.

## Performance decision: HOLD

Keep draft. The completed timing campaign does not establish a repeatable material complete-import gain. Four independent memory cells support small descriptive sampled-memory reductions; both JMdict memory cells remain unqualified. No all-corpus memory qualification or exact browser peak-memory claim is made.

[Run 45123053286](https://github.com/ManabiIO/manabitan/actions/runs/45123053286) completed all six cells and **252 fresh-profile imports**: six excluded warmups, twelve adjacent alternating candidate/parent pairs and six interleaved same-code C/A pairs per cell, with independent reversed-order replication. Independent source/package, fixture/work, raw operation-clock and statistical checks pass. Timing used Node 22.22.0 / Chromium 153.0.8010.12, identical production defaults and OPFS storage through the post-UI import-complete event. Twelve source-derived persisted probes and restart verification passed for every import.

Entries are **forward / reverse**; negative is faster. Equal work compares summed paired durations within one cell. No hosts are pooled and no control effects are subtracted.

| Jitendex | +0.37% / +1.73% | +0.22% / +1.60% | −0.53% / +0.66% | −4.26% / +0.99% |
| VNDB | −1.22% / −0.95% | +0.67% / −1.03% | −0.63% / +0.95% | −0.52% / +0.72% |

Its forward timing cohort retains two +12.05% / +13.07% slower pairs, yielding +0.67% equal work despite a favorable median interval. Reverse's median interval includes zero. JMdict and Jitendex are slower on equal work in both directions. Copy counters are overlapping worker-duration sums, not wall-time savings. Frozen timing study source: `9941723a323c76e8d73a16880e658fa243f17187`.

## Problem

The compressed native parser can reuse a glossary CRC only when it already has an exact byte-equality witness. The existing verifier splits CRC work at every unique row and applies a compression-ratio admission gate, so the pinned Jitendex workload still rechecks most glossary source bytes.

## Change

Keep each uninterrupted run of original source bytes contiguous and compute a separate glossary CRC only for an equality root that another row actually references. Flatten witness chains in the existing witness array, then reuse those proven CRCs. Incremental braided CRC accepts the preceding CRC state, with a small input-independent polynomial-power table.

The source-size and deflate constraints remain. Remove the compression-ratio admission gate so the same exact verifier can apply to low-compression groups. Original source CRC verification, exact equality, bank boundaries, monotonic row-span validation and errors before delivery to the sink remain enforced.

This creates no additional per-row verifier table. **Broader eligibility does activate the existing four-byte-per-reserved-row witness allocation for more inputs**, so memory remains a qualification gate.
